title: Database: SQLAlchemy or SQLModel, sessions and migrations
summary: An ORM maps classes to tables.

sections.definition: An ORM maps classes to tables. SQLAlchemy 2.0 is the standard in Python; SQLModel, by the same author as FastAPI, combines SQLAlchemy and Pydantic and is what the official documentation uses. The Session is the unit of work of a request: you accumulate changes and they are applied with commit(). Alembic versions the schema with migrations.
sections.analogy: The Session is a shopping cart: you add, change and remove, but nothing is charged until the commit. Migrations are the records of each remodel of the store: numbered, in order and reversible.
sections.problem: The N+1 problem (one query per row when accessing a relationship) and concatenating text into SQL are the two most-asked mistakes. And create_all() is no good for evolving the schema in production.
sections.code:example:
from sqlmodel import Field, Session, SQLModel, create_engine, select

class Producto(SQLModel, table=True):
    id: int | None = Field(default=None, primary_key=True)
    nombre: str = Field(index=True)
    precio: int
    stock: int = 0

# PostgreSQL con psycopg 3 (uv add "psycopg[binary]")
DATABASE_URL = "postgresql+psycopg://tienda:secreto@localhost:5432/tienda"
engine = create_engine(DATABASE_URL)

@app.post("/productos", status_code=201)
def crear_producto(datos: ProductoCrear, session: SessionDep) -> Producto:
    producto = Producto.model_validate(datos)
    session.add(producto)
    session.commit()
    session.refresh(producto)        # trae el id generado
    return producto

@app.get("/productos")
def listar(session: SessionDep, categoria: str | None = None) -> list[Producto]:
    consulta = select(Producto)
    if categoria:
        consulta = consulta.where(Producto.categoria == categoria)
    return session.exec(consulta).all()

# Migraciones
# uv add alembic
# uv run alembic init migrations
# uv run alembic revision --autogenerate -m "crear tabla productos"
# uv run alembic upgrade head
sections.bad:
pedidos = session.exec(select(Pedido)).all()
for p in pedidos:
    print(p.cliente.nombre)    # 1 consulta por pedido

session.exec(text(f"SELECT * FROM productos WHERE nombre = '{nombre}'"))

N+1 queries and SQL injection.
sections.good:
from sqlalchemy.orm import selectinload

consulta = select(Pedido).options(selectinload(Pedido.cliente))
pedidos = session.exec(consulta).all()   # 2 consultas en total

session.exec(select(Producto).where(Producto.nombre == nombre))

Eager loading and parameters bound by the ORM.
sections.bridge:typescript: SQLModel or SQLAlchemy ≈ TypeORM or Prisma; Alembic ≈ prisma migrate or TypeORM migrations. The Session resembles TypeORM's EntityManager: a unit of work that groups changes.
sections.interview: I use SQLAlchemy or SQLModel to map models to tables, with one database session per request injected as a dependency, which is closed when it finishes. I add objects to the session, commit and refresh to get the generated values. To avoid N+1 I load relationships with selectinload or joinedload, I never concatenate SQL, and I evolve the schema with hand-reviewed Alembic migrations, not with create_all in production.
sections.myths:
• Forgetting commit(): nothing gets saved.
  • Sharing a global session across requests.
  • Not reviewing the --autogenerate script: Alembic does not detect everything (for example, renames).
  • Mixing AsyncSession with a synchronous driver.

items.q: You did session.add(producto) and responded 201, but the product does not show up in the database. What was missing?
items.why: Without commit the transaction is discarded when the session closes.
